Studio Work


Anton Repponen is a New York–based interaction designer with over 20 years of experience creating products, digital experiences, and brand systems that people genuinely enjoy using.

He leads design at Anton & Irene, the studio he co-founded in 2014, where his practice spans product definition, UI/UX, visual design, motion, 3D, photography, sound, and video. His work combines clear information architecture with strong art direction and prototyping, with accessibility, performance, and craft treated as essentials rather than extras.

His projects have been featured by publishers such as Fast Company and Taschen and recognized with major industry honors, including Red Dot “Best of the Best.” The NU:RO watch he designed and produced was sold at the MoMA Design Store in New York. Beyond studio work, Anton speaks regularly at international conferences and teaches as co-chair of the Interaction Design program at Harbour.Space University in Barcelona and Bangkok.

M+ Museum

Website
Digital design dystem
Development oversight

2021-2022
For the opening of Hong Kong’s newest museum, designed by Herzog & de Meuron, we built its digital presence from the ground up rather than redesigning an existing site. From day one, accessibility shaped the system: clear information hierarchy, semantic markup for screen readers, keyboard-friendly navigation, and an optional high-contrast mode. A fully bilingual architecture treats English and Chinese equally, ensuring content parity and intuitive language switching for both local visitors and an international audience.

Project overview
MyTeam is an internal HR platform used by ~5,500 employees across multiple teams and regions, supporting engagement, feedback, and day-to-day interactions. While the product included multiple engagement features, the experience lacked coherence. Feedback signals were fragmented across different parts of the system, making it difficult to understand team dynamics and act on them. The work focused on structuring how feedback is captured, surfaced, and interpreted — aligning interaction patterns and making engagement more visible and actionable at scale.
Approach
Structuring feedback signals revealed that the issue wasn’t visibility — but how the system translates interactions into something meaningful.
